transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… things at home have been tense. My wife says I’m reading too much into it, but her late meetings and some little changes in her work messages… they’ve been lining up in ways that don’t feel accidental. It’s been going on a while, maybe a year. It feels like there’s something being signaled, like something she won’t just say directly.
Besides these suspicions about your wife, have you noticed anything unusual with your senses—like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or seeing things that others don't see?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t seen things or heard voices, if that’s what you mean. It’s more just… noticing what’s there.

Aside from your wife, do you find yourself generally suspicious or distrustful of other people in your life—like friends, coworkers, or family—and has that been a pattern for you going back many years, even before this situation with your wife?
No… not really. I mean, I keep to myself, but I wouldn’t say I’ve always been suspicious of everyone. This feels more… specific.

During this past year, have you also noticed periods of feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or low on energy—or on the flip side, unusually elevated, irritable, or full of energy—that lasted for a week or more?
Not really… I mean, I’ve been stressed, sure. Tired sometimes. But I wouldn’t say I’ve had, like, a week of being really low or unusually energetic or anything like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a circumscribed, well-systematized delusion of infidelity (jealousy-type delusion) focused specifically on his wife, persisting for about one year. There is no evidence of hallucinations, no pervasive suspiciousness/paranoia predating this episode (ruling out paranoid personality disorder), no mood episode symptoms (ruling out mood disorder with psychotic features), and no broader thought disorder or negative symptoms suggestive of schizophrenia. The delusion is isolated, non-bizarre, and encapsulated, with preserved functioning outside this specific belief system, consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22).
